To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the recombinant catalase-A from rice plant can be expressed in E. coli by employing a fusion partner thioredoxin, trigger factor and δ-aminolevic acid.

the recombinant catalase-A from rice plant was produced in soluble, active and bio-available form by using E. coli expression system, and the protein could be purified to homogeneity by simple and efficient protocol.

the specific requirement of thioredoxin and trigger factor protein along with low temperature treatment during the induction period and the supplementation of δ-amino levulinic acid are the key factors for synthesis of soluble and bio-active rice plant Catalase in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of recombinant plant catalase in its active form in prokayotic expression system.
the expression of a bio-active plant enzyme, catalase-A, using E. coli expression system.
the development of a simple protocol for the expression and purification of bio-active recombinants plant catalase-A using a heterologous expression host.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present method provides a simple and cost-effective way for production of soluble and bio-active plant catalase in E. coli.
the present method is the first report of a plant catalase being expressed in a prokaryotic host system as a soluble and active form.
the present protocol provides the first report of bio-active rice plant CAT-A synthesis in prokaryotes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the present study has provided the basis for a novel and simple strategy for the production of bio-active recombinants of plant proteins in E. coli.
the expression of catalase in prokaryotes is possible but requires the presence of a specific fusion partner, trigger factor and the supplementation of δ-amino-levulinic acid.
the present protocol would help in the production of bio-active plant proteins in E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recombinant catalase-A can be produced in soluble form in E. coli, which can be used for structural and functional studies of the plant enzyme.
the present protocol can be used to produce bio-active plant enzymes in recombinant Esch. coli.
the present protocol can be applied for the production of other plant catalase proteins.
